body.text: Run start 2026-11-18T09:36:23Z (authoritative status). Register the provided verified reconstruction unchanged and skip the reconstruction hour as explicitly required by demo2sim/RECONSTRUCTION.md. Then define demonstration-style criteria, construct a hardware-faithful simulator, prove feasibility, train the required single neural policy, and gate every retained change. No target rounds.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

body.text: Criteria v1 recorded as r0003 before simulation judgments. Initial CPU simulation uses actual 7-joint arm and supplied Wuji meshes with MuJoCo contact, 8-iteration differential IK and delayed commands. Reset palm chosen as package start (constant 1.5-s ramp) to keep starts visible and avoid motion during the hold-start check; the recommended overhead ramp lags by 32 mm in this articulated model. FK error 0.036 mm; initial supported hold and contract log checks pass. Teacher approach budget: 90 min for geometric opposed fingertip trajectory tracking, then reassess using actual contact/rotation results.

First exploratory teacher rollout, seed 0: no object contact before torque_halt at 4.63 s. I inspected top/right harness renders: the unused outstretched middle/ring/pinky fingers reach the table while the intended thumb-index pinch is still misaligned. Measured opposed_s=0 and max arm external torque 62.8 Nm. Curl unused digits and assess reachable approach choices; the geometric fingertip fit alone did not establish feasibility. 64/64 randomized supported hold starts passed, with no stops; sensor/contract consistency also passed on the saved hold episode.

Coupled contact IK gives sub-mm fingertip matches for seed 0 and ~1.5 mm for seed 5, but physical rollout 0 holds only 0.85 s, rises 25.6 mm, then pivots passively by 30.4 deg and drops; it does not meet the active-turn criterion. Render at 10 s confirms a thumb-index pinch. The teacher turn planner rotates the wrist 84.5 deg, so it needs an explicit wrist-rotation bound. Seed 5 hits the table during descent. Slow approach/settling, proper opposed normal forces, and mechanical joint-stop stiffness will be tested; default MuJoCo joint stops yielded 24–38 mrad past limits under contact, beyond the 20 mrad allowance.

Simulation validation caught a modeling error before registration: enabling all supplied hand convex hulls against one another caused 0/64 open holds to stay within hardware limits (the vendor hulls overlap around adjacent motor housings). The earlier 64/64 result applied to object contacts without full hand self collision and is not evidence for the failed variant. Replace inter-finger self contacts with phalange-core capsules, preserve full supplied hulls against objects, explicitly document the approximation, and repeat the supported-start and contract checks before freezing the evaluator.

body.text: Gate r0011 baseline: grasp_lift14/32, active turn0/32, success0/32,2 hardware violations; reproducible. Its review job failed because render_command expected state files in an output directory that the isolated render job starts empty. Repair the review command to reproduce selected episodes before calling the supplied renderer; keep physics, starts, predicates and criteria unchanged. Regenerate the two failing gate seeds locally and inspect them before retaining further teacher changes. Register task/feasibility suite v2 for this review-only repair.

I viewed the regenerated harness montage of gate r0011 seed1926376050 (top/left/right,0/4/8/12/16/20/24/28s). At12s the fingers reach the plug, but by16s the hand lifts away while the plug remains lying on the table; the turn is then attempted with no retained object. Earliest weakness is stable grasp retention, not terminal placement. CEM shooting improves local grip retention but still drops at turn. The turn transition must preserve the existing motor preload, and turn duration must keep real contacting-finger motion above the standard passive-speed threshold rather than merely moving slowly.

Shortening turn3–4s loses it earlier; the static contact plan develops14mm endpoint error and drives index joints to limits. These are training diagnostics, not task-suite results. I am checking the broad-face side pinch (seed5) separately. The original90-minute teacher approach budget ends11:16UTC; meanwhile prepare and validate a GPU copy of the same physical articulated model for a possible learned contact controller if geometric planning remains weak.

Expect holding success>.8 and progress beyond15deg; inspect results at budget end. GPU holding parity over128 perturbed states had median0.35mm/.76deg but p95=62mm/31deg, CPU/GPU held fractions .921/.825: it is not a passing full-task parity result. GPU training is exploratory; retain nothing on its scores alone, require CPU outcome checks and the full deployment gate before using a learned controller. Continue CPU physical CEM and grasp-posture improvements alongside it.

body.text: Local guarded-grasp CEM improves lift/style but then turns only28deg before dropping, versus the older black grasp53deg with a marginal palm posture and23deg passive lift drift. Thus grasp robustness alone is insufficient: contact placement and finger range during turn matter. Next physical branch will begin active finger turning during lift rather than allowing a fixed-finger gravitational pivot, and will seed privileged PPO from physical MPC actions. Budgets:300 updates each for the existing hold-first PPO and an MPC-initialized turn branch; no whole-task claim without frozen CPU gates.

Correction after recomputing frozen criteria on the exact old black seed5 physical prefix: its grasp DOES pass, palm72.5–72.6deg and lift stage at15.55s. The earlier >75deg concern applied to a different local grasp variant and should not be generalized. This old prefix instead accumulates22.6deg passive rotation, above20. The MPC-initialized privileged actor in a CPU held-state diagnostic reaches59.6deg active relative rotation and blades within6deg while continuously opposed, then loses thumb contact. Next: hand off during lift to replace the passive pivot with deliberate finger turning, and stabilize immediately at the qualified turn rather than continuing past it.

Full physical nominal black5 prefix with learned-teacher handoff17.0s meets grasp_lift and finger_turn at20.4s:67.9deg relative rotation,19.3deg passive,blade tilt19.97deg,palm70.73deg, hardware okay. Continuing the actor loses the result. Physical hold CEM predicts continuous opposed retention for1s at the valid-turn state. Allocate200PPO updates (~13.1M transitions) on idleGPU0 for a separate privileged retention teacher from this physically obtained turn state, goal0 hold2s; it is a teacher piece only and has no deployment/task score. Retention/carry must still pass the frozen CPU whole-task suite.
